subject: Climate & Environment
title: What Causes a Drought
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Causes a Drought usable.

hook.text: Drought is the slow disaster. It arrives without thunder and leaves only dust and hunger behind.

buildup.text: Persistent high-pressure systems block rain clouds from reaching a region for weeks or months.

discovery.text: Some droughts are worsened by El Niño — a warming of Pacific waters that shifts rainfall patterns.

twist.text: Unlike floods or hurricanes, drought has no clear start date. It creeps in slowly, noticed too late.

climax.text: Climate change is making droughts longer and more intense in already dry regions.

punchline.text: The most dangerous storms are the ones that never arrive.

quiz.question: What weather pattern commonly worsens droughts?

details.summary: Droughts occur when precipitation falls significantly below average for an extended period, depleting soil moisture, stream flow, and reservoirs. They can be triggered by persistent high-pressure systems, ocean temperature patterns, and are increasingly intensified by higher temperatures.
details.whyItMatters: Drought affects water supply, agriculture, energy, and ecosystems. Climate change is making droughts hotter, longer, and more frequent in many regions.
takeaways: Persistent high-pressure blocks steer rain-bearing storms away
Higher temperatures increase evaporation, intensifying drought
Droughts develop slowly but can persist for years or decades

faq.question: How does climate change make droughts worse?
faq.answer: Higher temperatures increase evaporation from soil and reservoirs, drying the land faster even without changes in rainfall. This means droughts start sooner, become more severe, and end more slowly than they would in a cooler climate.

faq.question: What is a flash drought?
faq.answer: A flash drought develops rapidly over weeks rather than months, typically when a heat wave coincides with low soil moisture. Crops can be destroyed before farmers recognize the severity, and there is little time for water conservation measures.
